source.title: PowerSGD: Practical Low-Rank Gradient Compression for Distributed Optimization
source.authors: Thijs Vogels; Sai Praneeth Karimireddy; Martin Jaggi

record.file_problem: Full paper text and appendices are supplied.
record.tranche_reason: It reports how gradient compression with error feedback and low-rank updates affects test performance in convolutional and recurrent models, extending generalization-related questions to distributed optimization. It does not directly test the listed versions’ central claims about memorization, architecture, optimizer choice, batch size, dropout, sharpness, or memorized examples.
record.gate_note: The study reports test accuracy or perplexity after applying gradient compression and compares these outcomes with SGD and other compressors. It does not test random-label memorization, width scaling, architecture comparisons, batch-size effects, dropout, generalization measures, or removal of memorized examples. Its discussion of low-rankness and generalization cites prior work and is not a new measurement of that relationship.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates gradient compression, not any supplied claim version. Its batch-size scaling experiments report runtime rather than held-out performance across batch sizes. The proposed connection to closing the large-batch generalization gap is speculative.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: PowerSGD reduces communication and training time while matching full-precision SGD held-out performance when its rank is sufficient. Its potential to close the large-batch generalization gap is a suggested future direction, not a demonstrated result.
record.recipe_differences: Distributed optimization with low-rank gradient compression and error feedback; evaluates test performance as a practical consequence, not the original interventions or measurements in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Compression rank changes test accuracy or perplexity; error feedback changes whether rank-4 PowerSGD converges to good accuracy; warm-start changes test accuracy. These are compression-method outcomes, not measurements of the listed versions.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 3 reports CIFAR-10 test accuracy of 94.3% for SGD and 93.6%, 94.4%, and 94.5% for PowerSGD ranks 1, 2, and 4. LSTM test perplexities are 91 for SGD and 102, 93, and 91 for those ranks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: With sufficient approximation rank, error-feedback low-rank gradient compression can match uncompressed SGD held-out performance within the same training budget.

record.problems: The experiments report test performance from three repetitions with min–max error bars for the default CIFAR-10 setup; the transformer case study uses one repetition. Hyperparameters such as momentum, weight decay, and learning-rate schedule were not tuned for any experiment. The paper does not directly measure any claim version’s specified behavior.
record.rows_left_out: No rows qualify: the measured outcomes are compression-method test performance and runtime, not outcomes for any listed claim version. Results in Tables 1–9 and Figures 4–7 are therefore not extracted as rows.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting alongside natural-label and random-label held-out accuracy.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning; compression algorithms are not this comparison.
Held-out performance across batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets and recipes that remove a batch-size penalty.
Effects of adding or removing dropout.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Removing highly memorized examples versus randomly selected examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The empty row set is appropriate for V1–V8. Learning rates were tuned; momentum, weight decay, and learning-rate schedules were not. Appendix D's transformer dataset is WikiText-103 according to Table 8, despite inconsistent WikiText-2 references elsewhere.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparison.
Large-batch generalization gap under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness or other generalization-gap measures.
Removal and retraining of memorized examples.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
